Subject: East Coast pilot: resource ask + architecture options for private hosting

Team —

Quick context: Nimbus Tech (POC customer) wants an East Coast pilot for a VPC/private-hosted instance to support early production traffic for a regulated vertical. They want a 6-week pilot with a potential commit afterwards. Sales (Nina) asked for a feasibility readout and a concise resource ask by EOD Monday so they can lock in a procurement window.

I need two things from this thread:
1) A short recommendation (A/B/C) on architecture approach we should propose to Nimbus (see the matrix attached). Options are: a) Fully isolated VPC with dedicated GPUs in partner colo, b) Redwood-managed VPC in partner cloud with customer peering, or c) Hosted with strict tenancy controls + SOC evidence (least preferred by customer).
2) A clear, minimal resourcing ask (eng, infra, oncall, SRE time) and a short risks list that Nina can share with procurement.

I attached a quick capacity estimate and an option matrix. Please reply inline with a single-paragraph recommendation and the headcount or FTE-weeks you expect for the pilot. If you think we need a quick 30-min huddle, propose two slots (I prefer Monday morning).

Thanks —
Michael
VP Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot_capacity_estimate.xlsx (xlsx), vpc-onprem-option-matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: East Coast pilot: resource ask + architecture options for private hosting

Michael / all —

Recommendation: Option B (Redwood-managed VPC in partner cloud with customer peering) as the primary proposal, with Option A (fully isolated in partner colo) as the contingency if Nimbus requires physical separation or stricter contractual controls. Option B hits the balance between isolation and speed-to-launch.

Rationale (short):
- Option B lets us leverage existing cloud networking for rapid setup (48–72 hrs for a staging-to-prod stack) and reduces device-level ops.
- Option A increases latency for setup and requires partner colo contracts + dedicated rack ops; it's defensible for regulated data but >3x resource/time compared to B.

Resource ask (pilot — 6 weeks):
- 0.6 FTE architecture lead (Karthik) for design + kickoff (approx 2 weeks full-time equivalent in week 0–1).
- 1 SRE (0.2 FTE across 6 weeks) to own initial deployment and runbook.
- 0.5 infra engineer (partner onboarding, peering, infra-as-code templates).
- 1 on-call rotation slot added to existing roster for the pilot window (predictable ~4 hrs/week overhead).
- Security/Compliance: 0.2 compliance engineer to assemble evidence packages and run SOC checklist.

Top risks: peering ACLs delaying traffic cutover; partner cloud quotas for GPUs; SLA expectations mismatch if customer expects zero degradation.

If we need to accelerate to Option A, add: +1 infra engineer full-time for 3 weeks and +1 on-call for initial run.

Happy to join a 30-min sync. Monday slots: 09:30–10:00 or 14:00–14:30 (ET).

—Karthik
Principal Architect

Thanks Karthik — I agree with Option B as default. A couple of ask additions from Product/CS perspective:

- We need a short SLA appendix for the pilot (target latency, availability window, maintenance windows) — can someone draft a 1-page we can attach to the PO? (Grace? Sean?)
- Minimal telemetry: we must expose token-level cost and per-route latency dashboards for the pilot. That will be used both by Nimbus and by our post-pilot evaluation. (Engineering: is the existing telemetry export ready for a partner cloud without extra work?)
- Pricing: propose a two-part charge: fixed platform fee for reserved capacity + variable per-token for overage. Sales (Nina) will negotiate numbers but we should present a default.

For the ask list to procurement: please include a short 'rollback plan' statement (how we'll scale back to hosted if we encounter compliance or perf issues).

I'll volunteer to draft the SLA appendix and the rollback blurb if someone provides the telemetry checklist and a tentative price range.

—Laura
Director, Product Management

Looping Nina in with the recommended approach and the minimal telemetry checklist attached.

Summary for Nimbus (short):
- Proposal: Redwood-managed VPC in partner cloud + customer peering (Option B).
- Timeline: provision and staging in 72 hours once PO signed; pilot baseline 6 weeks.
- Minimal resourcing: design lead (Karthik) + infra + SRE + security support as outlined.
- Deliverables: 1-page SLA appendix (Laura), telemetry dashboard (exported to Nimbus view), runbook + rollback plan.

Attachments: minimal_telemetry_checklist.md (md)

Nina — welcome. Can you confirm whether Nimbus requires contract language for data residency (physical) or if contractual assurances around handling and audit logs are sufficient? If it's purely contractual, Option B remains valid; if they require data to remain on-prem/within specific racks we will escalate to Option A and need the extra infra hours.

—Grace

We do NOT require physical rack guarantees for the pilot — contractual assurances and audit logs will be acceptable for this phase. That said, the customer expects clear SLA targets for latency during business hours and a documented rollback plan.

Next steps from our side: Finance needs the two-part pricing example and procurement wants the 1-page SLA appendix to attach to the PO. We plan to sign the PO on Wednesday if we have materials.
